annotationRules.materiality: Assign a topic only when it performs or receives the action, materially changes, supplies the necessary event setting, or passes a verified conditional implication rule.
annotationRules.evidence: Exact evidence must be a substring of normalized headline-plus-snippet text. Inferred evidence must name its reviewed rule.
annotationRules.incidental: Historical background, boilerplate, navigation, publisher tags, quotations unrelated to the current event, and keyword substrings are rejected.
annotationRules.coreTopic: A directly evidenced material subject that equivalent coverage must resolve to the same canonical topic ID.
annotationRules.secondaryTopic: A materially supported topic that may differ across publications because of article emphasis.

stabilityScenarios.rule: Identical content, registry, classifier, and policy versions reuse the prior validated assignment without a new model call.
Changing the primary source preserves cluster ID, effective topics, thread references, curator locks, and public URLs.
Merging duplicates preserves a surviving cluster, redirects predecessors, and reconciles rather than unions assignments.
Splitting a mixed cluster records lineage and reevaluates assignments for each successor without silently copying curator decisions.
A correction or retraction creates an auditable desired-state diff; stale automated topics can be removed while history remains immutable.
Different model output for the same uncached evidence cannot directly add or remove an effective public assignment.
